To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the instanton vacuum approach to QCD sum rules is a viable and useful tool in the study of the QCD vacuum; it is capable of producing results that are in agreement with those from the lattice; and, in the context of our study, it provides the first estimate of the power (1/q2-) corrections to Bjorken sum rules for Fν1.

the instanton vacuum provides an accurate description of power corrections in the Bjorken and Gross–Llewelyn–Smith sum rules; and that direct measurements of neutrino structure functions at a neutrino-factory would allow for an extraction of αs with reduced theoretical uncertainty.

the following topics: - The neutrino-nucleon cross section in the framework of the instanton vacuum. - The neutrino structure functions F2νp and F2νn at a neutrino-nucleus scattering. - The power corrections in the instanton model to the Bjorkenn sum rule.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Bjorken and Gross–Llewillyn-Smith sum rules provide a unique and complementary method to determine αs, and that the instanton vacuum is an important tool in this respect.
the Bjorken and Gross–Llewelynn-Smith sum rules, together with the QCD instanton vacuum model, allow one to determine αs to within ±0.0005 at Q2 = 10 GeV2.
the Bjorken and Gross–Llewillyn-Smith sum rules are not only the best, but also the most accurate, methods for determining the strong coupling constant αs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the power correction in the Bjorken (and Gross–Llewillyn-Smith) sum rule is small and can be neglected.
the Bjorken (and Gross–Llewelyn-Smith) sum rules are not spoiled by power corrections and that they can be used for an accurate determination of αs.
the instanton vacuum is a good model of the vacuum of QCD, and the power corrections to the sum rules are under control.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for the first time, the QCD sum rules for the twist-4 operator are in agreement with a model calculation, and that the model result can be used to reduce the theoretical uncertainty in the extraction of αs in the neutrino sector.
the instanton-induced corrections to the Bjokren sum rule are small and can be neglected in the analysis of the experimental data.

, in order to extract the strong coupling constant from the Bjorken and Gross–Llewelyn–Smith sum rules with the precision of a few per cent, one needs to know the Q2-dependences of the twist-4 operators with the accuracy better than a few per cent.
